neighbours.label: an object pronoun (him, them, these) after a verb or preposition, pointing back to someone or something named earlier
fire: In 1975 the old farmer leased the orchard to him for ten years.
The tutors were patient, and the students learned a lot from them.
After the trial, the village elders were chosen by him personally.
The council sold the land to them at a very low price.
When the twins arrived, the teacher sat next to them at lunch.
The mayor praised the firefighters and thanked them in public.
Margaret wrote to the bishop and later received a reply from him.
Two new weeds appeared, and the spray had no effect on these.
quiet: In 1975 the old farmer leased the orchard to his son for ten years.
The tutors were patient, and the students learned a lot in class.
After the trial, the village elders were chosen by vote.
The council sold the land to a developer at a very low price.
When the twins arrived, the teacher sat by the window at lunch.
The mayor praised the firefighters for their quick response.
Margaret wrote to the bishop and later received a reply by post.
Two new weeds appeared, and the spray had no effect at all.

notes: Top peaks ' them' x8, ' him' x4, ' it', ' this', ' these'. Probe: 'sold the business to him' 0.43, 'from them' 0.14, same with a noun object 0.04.
